Now that your PR is merged, here's an updated entry:
 
Open-source contributor: DIP (Development Intelligence Platform), VXU Labs · Oct 2026
github.com/vxu-labs/dip, PR #5 (merged)

* Ran a keyboard accessibility audit of the project's web dashboard, covering focus order, visible focus, accessible names and dialog focus. I reported two reproducible defects with control runs and screenshots, and the maintainer accepted the scope of the fix.
* Fixed a bug where background project updates erased in-progress text and dropped keyboard focus in the task details dialog. Unsaved input, focus, cursor position and scroll position are now kept across re-renders, while real data updates still show (JavaScript).
* Added a Playwright browser regression test that fails on the old code and passes with the fix. Verified it alongside the project's full suite (148 tests passing) before the maintainer merged it.

Skills to list: JavaScript, Node.js, Playwright, web accessibility (WCAG, keyboard and focus management), Git/GitHub, open-source workflow (fork, PR, DCO sign-off).
Keep it accurate:

* Credit: the maintainer added a follow-up commit and 14 extra test cases. Don't claim those; your part was the audit, the original fix and the original test.
* Scale: DIP is a new, small project. Say "open-source contributor", not anything implying an employer or a well-known company.
* Finding 2: if you do the follow-up PR, add a line for it. Two merged PRs reads better than one.

Be ready to explain in an interview:

* why replacing HTML with `innerHTML` loses focus and typed text;
* how you proved the bug was real (control runs) and that the test catches it (it fails without the fix);
* the edge case the maintainer caught (a slow save clearing newer text), and what you'd do differently. Interviewers often like hearing what you learned from a code review.

If you tell me your resume's format, such as a one-line bullet style or a separate Projects section, I can tighten this to fit.
